You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task note: paired rulers with marker projections

Observed on task-114588b6, verified by the correct final submission (1 demo / 2 demos / 3 demos / 4 demos all same rule).

## Rule
- A uniform background contains two equal-length, same-color straight guide bars (“rulers”), typically parallel but spatially offset, plus isolated pixels of a distinct marker color.
- Dots adjacent to/in the strip extending from one guide encode selected ruler positions: compare a dot's coordinate along the bar axis with the guide's start to get its index. For each selected index, fill the corresponding position on the other guide completely across the perpendicular span, using the dot color.
- Also extend each dot in a straight line toward its nearby/source guide (along the perpendicular axis), painting the intervening cells in the dot color. Recolor the original dot to color 4. Preserve the guide bars and all unrelated background cells.
- This applies in either orientation: horizontal guides => selected columns are projected to the opposite guide and dot trails are vertical; vertical guides => selected rows project to opposite guide and dot trails are horizontal. Use the relative index along each guide, not absolute coordinates, when transferring a selected position. The filled full-span projections can include canvas cells beyond the guide’s end where the opposite guide is offset.

## Concrete verified task instance
Input was 21x27, background 8, guide color 9. Left vertical ruler at column 0, rows 4–11; right ruler at column 26, rows 13–20. Marker color 3 points: (r,c) = (4,17), (6,21), (7,2), (9,22), (10,5), (11,17), zero-based.
- Each marker extends horizontally left to the left ruler in its own row: color intervening cells 3; marker becomes 4.
- Their ruler-relative indices from the left ruler (0,2,3,5,6,7) select matching rows of the right ruler: rows 13,15,16,18,19,20. Fill each selected row in color 3 across columns 0–25; keep column 26 guide color 9.
- Other cells remain 8; guide bars remain 9.

## Demo checks
- Horizontal example with top guide at row 0 and bottom guide at row 17: bottom-guide-aligned dots select corresponding top-guide indices; marker trails go vertically to the nearby guide; selected top slots fill the full interval toward the other guide.
- Vertical test is the rotated counterpart. Dots lie along the left guide’s axis; corresponding right-side ruler positions receive full horizontal fills. Preserve asymmetric offsets and compute indices relative to guide starts.
